definitions.explanation: An honorific term used to refer to someone else's son, showing respect toward the person being addressed and their family. Never used for one's own son.

examples.japanese: ご{子息|しそく}はお{元気|げんき}ですか。
ご{子息|しそく}が{大学|だいがく}に{合格|ごうかく}されたそうですね。
examples.english: I hear your son passed the university entrance exam.

examples.japanese: ご{子息|しそく}が{立派|りっぱ}に{成長|せいちょう}されて、さぞお{喜|よろこ}びのことでしょう。
examples.english: Your son has grown into a fine person — you must be very proud.

notes:
Composed of the honorific prefix ご and {子息|しそく} (son). This is a formal, respectful way to refer to another person's son, typically used in business settings, formal letters, and polite conversation with social superiors. For one's own son, use the humble term {愚息|ぐそく} or simply {息子|むすこ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ご{子息|しそく}の{就職|しゅうしょく}: your son's employment
- ご{子息|しそく}の{結婚|けっこん}: your son's marriage
- ご{子息|しそく}にもよろしく: please give my regards to your son

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {息子|むすこ}さん: your son — polite but less formal than ご{子息|しそく}
- {御令息|ごれいそく}: your son — even more formal and literary
- {愚息|ぐそく}: my (foolish) son — humble term for one's own son

REGISTER:
Used in formal and business contexts. In everyday conversation, {息子|むすこ}さん is more natural.
